newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina sees 1996/97 oil price at $20/barrel.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina sees 1996/97 oil price at $20/barrel.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Thursday it expected the average price of Indonesia oil will be about $20 per barrel in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending March.

"I think the average oil price in our oil in 1996/97 will be higher than the budgeted $16.50 per barrel. I think we will reach an average of $20," Pertamina president-director Faisal Abda'oe told reporters.

"For every one-dollar increase above the price envisaged in the budget, Indonesia will receive around $600 million," he said. "But Indonesia must pay (higher prices) for crude oil and fuel products it imports."
Indonesia imports crude oil from the Middle East for its refinery in Cilacap, Central Java, to produce lubricants.

Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said in statement to a parliamentary commission hearing on Thursday Indonesia produces 1.585 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil and condensates.
Indonesia has an OPEC (Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries) quota of 1.330 million bpd of oil.
"The production includes 64,300 bpd we use in the oil fields," he said, without giving details.
Pertamina sources said the Duri field in Central Sumatra operated by PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia uses about 60,000 bpd in its steam flooding operations.
PT Caltex is jointly owned by Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc of the United States.
Abda'oe said Indonesia exported around 700,000 bpd.
Minister Sudjana also said the average price of Indonesian oil was $23.14 per barrel in December and $22.46 in November.
Indonesia has set a price of $16.50 a barrel in its 1997/98, unchanged from 1996/97.
